To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

clinical supervision should be conducted in an environment of trust and mutual respect, and that it should be available when it is required, in the form that is required, and that the supervisor and supervisee should have a good match.
clinical supervision is an effective way for occupational therapists to develop their professional knowledge and skills.

clinical supervision is an important component of occupational therapist professional support and is best achieved when the supervisor and the supervisee have a positive supervisory relationship and the supervisor is readily available for support in between sessions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to make clinical supervision effective and sustainable in practice contexts, particularly for health professionals in dispersed communities such as Australia.
the importance of matching and fit between supervisor and supervisee, the role of the supervisory relationships and the need for a balance between face-to-face and telesupervisory contact.
clinical supervision as an important aspect of professional development for occupational therapists
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

clinical supervision should be provided by an appropriately trained supervisor with whom a good supervisory relationship has been established and who is readily accessible for support in between supervision sessions.
the enablers and barriers to high-quality clinical supervision are complex and multifaceted.
clinical supervision needs to be a relationship based, flexible and responsive process that is tailored to the needs of supervisees and their work contexts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

clinical supervision needs to be conducted in a supportive, trusting environment where the supervisor and the supervisee can work together to identify the supervisee’s professional learning needs and develop an appropriate learning plan.
high quality clinical supervision is perceived to be associated not only with the supervisor-supervisee relationship, but also with the supervisor-supervisor match.
the enablers and barriers identified in our research could be applied to other health professions and other countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of clinical relationships is key to the success of clinical supervision.
the relationship between the supervisor and supervisee is the key to high quality clinical and professional support.
the supervisory relationship is key.
